app.title: SatVision Cerrado — vegetation detection and two-date change map
app.summary: A person picks a satellite image, either uploaded or chosen from a folder of processed scenes. They tune colour thresholds or switch to an automatic vegetation index, and see the image beside a vegetation mask overlay with the share of vegetated pixels and a classifier's vegetation-or-deforestation prediction. For one area, they choose a base year and a comparison year. The same thresholds mask both images, and each pixel is classed as lost, gained, stable or never vegetated. A change heatmap shows this, with pixel counts, percentages and, if a pixel size is entered, hectares. The heatmap can be saved as an image file.

task.text: Measure how much vegetation an area lost or gained between two image dates by thresholding each image into a vegetation mask and differencing the masks.

data.text: RGB satellite image tiles, organised either by land-cover class or by area with one image per year
data.item: a satellite image tile of one area at one date

stage.text: measuring vegetation change between two dates once imagery is prepared, before reporting

mechanism.text: Sidebar controls choose the image and set the threshold parameters. The same parameters drive both the single-image mask overlay and the two-date change map. Side-by-side panes show the original against the mask, and base year against comparison year against a change heatmap, with numeric totals below.

field.text: vegetation masking and multitemporal change detection in satellite remote sensing

workflow.name: detect change between two dates of the same scene and quantify it

steps.here: choose a dataset, then upload a JPG/PNG or pick a class/area folder and an image from it; nothing renders until an image is loaded

steps.step: set how the target is detected
steps.here: sliders for hue min/max, saturation min and value min define an HSV vegetation range; a radio switches to an automatic excess-green index thresholded by Otsu

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: the original image is shown beside a coloured mask overlay titled with percent vegetation, with a CNN's vegetation/deforestation prediction and class confidences
choose an area and a base year and comparison year; both images appear with their own prediction next to a heatmap colouring each pixel as stable, lost, gained or never vegetated
pixel counts and percentages for loss, gain, stable and none, vegetation % per year and the difference; entering metres per pixel adds hectares
a save button writes the change heatmap as a PNG named by area and the two years

distinctive: the same manually tuned colour thresholds are applied to both dates, so the change map depends on one shared definition of the target
every pixel falls into one of four transition classes (loss, gain, stable, absent in both), each counted and coloured
an optional ground resolution in metres per pixel converts pixel counts into hectares
a pretrained two-class image classifier's prediction is shown beside the threshold-based mask as an independent check
an automatic index-plus-Otsu threshold is offered as an alternative to manual HSV ranges
